name_devanagari: उमामहेश्वर मन्दिर  (built in 1655 CE) ll KIR0006
description_en: This pagoda-style three-storey Umāmaheśvara Mandira is situated at the highest point (around 1414 m) of Kirtipur. It is also known as Kvāḥcva Degaḥ amongst the local community, meaning situated in the highest point. One can view almost the entire valley from this place. This site used to be a fort in middle ages, making it then not only religiously but also geopolitically significant.Viśvanātha Bābu from Tumbāhāḥ, Patan built this temple in 1655 CE (NS 775).[1]According to the copperplate inscription in the temple, he had also established aguṭhīto maintain and renovate the temple as well as to perform the rituals (cf.D. VajrācāryaVS 2056, 495). On the contrary of this inscription,Bernier(1978, 144) erroneously suggests that it was a four-storey temple built in 1673 CE.S. Tivārī(2013, 29) agrees that it was originally a four-storey temple. While there is no documented evindence to verify this claim, the present-day structure and remains of the temple do not affirm this argument either (also cp.Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, 49).The temple was gradually decorated and renovated following its initial construction. A pair of lions were installed to the left and to the right of the staircase leading to the temple in 1662 CE (NS 782). A stone entrance to the temple's courtyard was built in 1715 CE (NS 835). The plinths of the temple were renovated in 1717 CE (NS 839). The roof of the temple can be seen completely damaged in the 1850s painting of Henry Ambrose Oldfield (see,http://www.bl.uk/onlinegallery/onlineex/apac/other/019wdz000002844u00000000.html; accessed on 21.10.2020). It is probable that the temple collapsed during the 1833 CE earthquakes and was not renovated until 1850s. It was again destroyed by the 1934 CE earthquakes but then was immediately renovated by Jagata Bahādura Pradhāna (known as Sipāĩ Bāje) using corrugated pewter sheets for its roof. During that earthquake, the clock tower of Kathmandu, built by Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera, was also destroyed. During its renovation, one of its four bell clocks was brought to this temple.In 1947 CE, the pinnacle, crowning the third floor of the temple, was damaged by a heavy storm. Since no renovation work took place back then, the temple remained two-storey for the next thirty five years. In 1982 CE, the thenPradhānapañca(head of the village council) Rudra Bahādura Pradhāna, restored its third-storey and tiled its roof with thejhĩgaṭībricks with the support of the local community (cf.Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, 50). The Kirtipur Metropolitan Office and the local community jointly adorned the temple in 2007 CE by carving its plain pillars and struts.Neither theguṭhī(established by Viśvanātha who initially built the temple) is active, nor any religious or social events take place in the temple in the present-day. It is in a socially abandoned state of condition. Even the elderly people cannot recall any events and practices which used to take place in the temple.Footnotes^H. Jośī(VS 2029, 56) misinforms us that this temple was built by the Pradhānas ofDathutaḥjhyāḥ, Patan.
description_ne: कीर्तिपुरको सबैभन्दा उचो भागमा यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । मन्दिरलाई स्थानीयले बोलीचालीमा 'क्वाःच्व देगः' भन्दै आएका छन् । 'उमामहेश्वर मन्दिर' केही दशक अघि मात्र प्रचारमा आएको नाम हो । 'क्वाःच्व देगः'को अर्थ उचो भागमा अवस्थित किल्लामा बनेको मन्दिर भन्ने हुन्छ । उपत्यकाका अधिकांश भू–भाग देख्न सकिने उच्च स्थान भएकोले मध्यकालमा यो ठाउँ सामरिक दृष्टिले निकै महत्वपूर्ण थियो । यसर्थ यो ठाउँमाँ मध्यकालमा किल्ला हुने गरेको तथ्य कीर्तिपुरमा प्राप्त विभिन्न अभिलेखहरूबाट थाहा हुन्छ । किल्लाको रूपमा रहेको उचो स्थलमा सन् १६५५ (नेसं ७७५) मा तुम्बाहाःका (पाटन) पात्र वंश विश्वनाथ बाबुले यो मन्दिर बनाउन लगाएका हुन् । निर्माण पश्चात् उनले मन्दिरको वार्षिक कर्म र मर्मत सम्भारको लागि विभिन्न ठाउँमा जग्गा छुट्याई गुठी गठन गरेको तथ्य मन्दिर भित्र हुने गरेको  ताम्रपत्रमा उल्लेख छ  (D. VajrācāryaVS 2056, 495)।बर्नियरले यो मन्दिरको स्थापना सन् १६७३ मा भएको र प्रारम्भमा यो चार तल्लाको हुने गरेको भनेका छन् (Bernier1978, 144) । त्यसैगरी सुदर्शनराज तिवारीले पनि यसलाई चार तल्लाकै भएको स्वीकारेका छन् छन् (S. Tivārī2013, 29) । उग्रचण्डी देवी र हरिसिद्धि देवीको मन्दिर बाहेक चार तल्ले मन्दिरको अस्तित्व नेपाल उपत्यकामा नभएको र चार तल्लाको मानी पुनर्मिलान (refit) गर्दा हाल बचेको पुरानो भागसंग मेल नखाने भएकोले ठोस प्रमाणबिना चार तल्ले थियो भनी स्वीकार्न सकिदैन (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, 49)  । मन्दिरमा भएको ताम्रपत्रबाट बर्नियरले मन्दिर सन् १६७३ मा निर्माण भएको भनी लेखेको कुरा गलत ठहर्छ । त्यसैगरी विश्वनाथ बाबुले बनाएको यो मन्दिरलाई हरिराम जोशीले गल्तीवस् पाटन दथुतःझ्याः टोलका प्रधानहरूले बनाएको भनेका छन् (H. JośīVS 2029, 56)।मन्दिर निर्माण पछि मन्दिरमा विभिन्न वस्तु थप्ने र प्राङ्गणलाई सुन्दरीकरण गर्ने कार्य हुँदै गयो । सन् १६६२ (नेसं ७८२) मा मन्दिरको खुड्किलोको दायाँ–बायाँ एक जोडा हात्ती स्थापना गरियो । सन् १७१५ (नेसं ८३५) मा मन्दिरको प्राङ्गणमा प्रवेश गर्ने ढुङ्गाको द्वार बनाइयो भने  सन् १७१७ (नेसं ८३९) मा मन्दिरको तीन तहको पेटी मर्मत गरियो । सन् १८५० देखि १८५५ को बीचमा ए.एच ओल्डफिल्डद्वारा कोरिएको चित्रमा यो मन्दिरको छानो पूर्णतः भत्की दलिनहरू लथालिङ्गको अवस्थामा रहेको देख्न सकिन्छ (http://www.bl.uk/onlinegallery/onlineex/apac/other/019wdz000002844u00000000.html) । यसबाट सन् १८३३ को भूकम्पमा यो मन्दिर भत्की दशकौं सम्म पनि पुनःनिर्माण हुन नसकेको देखिन्छ । सन् १९३४ को अर्को महाभूकम्प पश्चात् तत्कालीन द्वारे जगतबहादुर प्रधान (सिपाइँ बाजे) को पहलमा जस्तापाताबाट छानो छाई जेनतेन मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । यसै जीर्णोद्धारको क्रममा वीर शम्शेरद्वारा निर्मित घण्टाघर भूकम्पमा भत्केकोले त्यहाँ भएका चार घण्टामध्ये एक यस मन्दिरमा ल्याई स्थापना गरिएको थियो । सन् १९४७ मा ठुलो हुरी चली मन्दिरको माथिल्लो तल्ला र गजूर खसे पश्चात ३५ वर्षसम्म मन्दिर २ तल्लाको रूपमै रह्यो । सन् १९८२ मा तत्कालीन प्रधानपञ्च रुद्रबहादुर प्रधानको पहलकद्मी र स्थानीयको सहयोगमा मन्दिर पुनः तीन तले बनाई झिंगटीबाट छाइएको थियो (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057, 50) । सन् २००६ मा नगरपालिका र स्थानीयको संयुक्त प्रयासबाट मन्दिरमा विगत प्रयोग भएका सादा थामो र टुँडालका ठाउँमा बुट्टेदार काष्ठ सामग्री प्रयोग गरी मन्दिरको सौंदर्यीकरण गरिएको थियो ।मन्दिर निर्माता विश्वनाथ बाबुले मन्दिरको लागि प्रसस्त जग्गा छुट्याई विभिन्न वार्षिक कर्मको उल्लेख गरे तापनि हाल मन्दिरसंग सम्बन्धित कुनैपनि गुठी एवं वार्षिक कर्महरू अस्तित्वमा छैनन् । मन्दिरसंग सम्बन्धित गुठी कहिले लोप हुन पुग्यो र गुठीबाट यहाँ के–कस्ता धार्मिक–सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि हुने गर्दथे भन्ने कुरामा कोही पनि स्थानीय बृद्ध–बृद्धाहरू जानकार छैनन् ।

historical_events.event_description: The roof of the temple can be seen completely damaged in the 1850s painting of Henry Ambrose Oldfield (see,http://www.bl.uk/onlinegallery/onlineex/apac/other/019wdz000002844u00000000.html; accessed on 21.10.2020). It is probable that the temple collapsed during the 1833 CE earthquakes and was not renovated until 1850s.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a Pair of Elephant Statues
historical_events.event_description: The temple can be accessed through a long flight of stone steps flanked by two stone elephants installed in 1662 CE. They are about five-feet tall including the remains of the broken riding figures on top of them.
Laṣkmīnātha Bābu (a younger brother of Viśvanātha who initiated the construction of the temple) installed the statue of Umāmaheśvara in the sanctum.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the First Viṣṇu Statue (A)
historical_events.event_description: Someśvara Bābu installed the first Viṣṇu statue in the sanctum in the memory of Viśveśvara Bābu.
It is probable that Someśvara Bābu offered something to the temple. Since the last line of the inscription recording the event can hardly be deciphered, its content remains unclear.
In the memory of late Triratna and Rāmayāyā Maharajana, their son Surjamāna and other family members offered a brass banner (patāḥ) to the temple.
In the memory of late Triratna and Rāmayāyā Maharajana, their son Surjamāna and other family members offered the brassmaṇḍalato the temple.
The Kirtipur Metropolitan Office and the local community jointly adorned the temple in 2006 CE by carving its plain pillars and struts.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the Second Viṣṇu Statue (B)
historical_events.event_description: Someśvara Bābu installed the second Viṣṇu statue in the sanctum.
The temple was again destroyed by the 1934 CE earthquakes but then was immediately renovated by Jagata Bahādura Pradhāna (known as Sipāĩ Bāje) using corrugated pewter sheets for its roof.
In 1947 CE, the pinnacle, crowning the third floor of the temple, was damaged by a heavy storm.
The temple was renovated by the Lāyekū Village Pañcāyata in collaboration with the local community and the Pañcāyata Ministry.
The stone gate of the temple was constructed in 1715 CE.
The plinths of the temple were renovated in 1719 CE.

historical_events.event_name: Initial Construction, Land Grant, and Establishment of a Guṭhī
historical_events.event_description: The temple was constructed by Viśvanātha Bābu from Tumbāhāḥ, Patan. He also endowed some land to maintain the temple as well as established aguṭhīto perform its annual rituals.

According to the local memory, the original bell of this temple was stolen by people from Bhaktapur. The original bell is also missing in the watercolour painting by Oldfield (1855 CE).The contemporary bell was installed following the 1994 CE earthquakes. This bell is originally a quarter striking bell from the previous Ghaṇṛāghara built by Bīra Śamsera. When the clock tower collapsed during the 1994 CE earthquakes, then prime minister, Juddha Śamsera, gave the bell at the request of current Dvāre of Kirtipur, Jagata Bahādura Pradhāna (also known as Sipāhi Bājyā). The inscription on the bell records that it had been cast by Gillet and Johnstone Founders of Croydon, England in 1895 CE.
